dedupe_keys.name: chemical leasing ch l and the sherwood plot

description: The study develops a microeconomic model of chemical-leasing contracts for recovering valuable compounds from wastewater. Its Sherwood-plot representation relates recovery cost to compound dilution. The authors model allocation of payoffs through three contract-pricing systems, with profitability limits and market types based on available cost-efficiency information. A Kullback–Leibler divergence metric represents market dominance. This is a formal economic model tied to physical resource-recovery processes, not proof of an operating leasing market or publicly available solver. It builds on the separately described resource-recovery Sherwood model; actual contract terms, code and numerical case coverage remain unknown. The source describes the stated resource-recovery analysis. The source authors provide this description through Zenodo, whose deposit declares CC BY 4.0 and public document access. Geographic and temporal coverage remain limited to the cases or observations explicitly described. Only metadata and file descriptors were reviewed; no document, measurements, model archive or code was read. Related components retain their source identities and uncertain experimental overlap. Document access and licensing do not establish executable availability or software rights.
